findings.quote: | Default FIFO queue throughput | More needs a standard queue |
findings.type: technical: wrong decision rule (refuted by verified facts)
findings.evidence: Verified facts sqs-fifo-ht-top-regions-70000-tps and sqs-fifo-ht-top-regions-batched-700000, source quotas-messages: "For high throughput mode, these API request limits are as follows: ... US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), and Europe (Ireland): Up to 70,000 transactions per second (TPS)." and "Up to 700,000 messages per second (10x the non-batch limit of 70,000 TPS)." Also sqs-fifo-ht-other-regions-2400-tps ("All other AWS Regions: Default throughput of 2,400 TPS"). The cited fact sqs-faq-fifo-default-throughput-3000-with-batching-300-without is scoped 'per FIFO queue, default mode'. More than 3,000 messages per second does not require a standard queue: high throughput mode for FIFO queues keeps order per group at far higher rates. An exam option 'enable high throughput for the FIFO queue' would be ruled out by this row, and the reader would give a founder wrong advice. Fix: 'More: turn on high throughput mode (FIFO keeps order) or use a standard queue', with a link to sqs-fifo-ht-top-regions-70000-tps; consider one line in the FIFO subsection (step 4 'Rate') naming high throughput mode.
findings.resolution: fix-31: A-list row now 'More: high throughput mode' (no number, so no new A-list fact); FIFO step 4 adds 'High throughput mode allows more: in three Regions, up to [70,000 transactions per second](sqs-fifo-ht-top-regions-70000-tps)'; 1-fast FIFO throughput cell adds 'more with high throughput mode' and the deciding question no longer presents the default as the ceiling; card c007 extra and speak s03 follow-up name high throughput mode.

findings.section: signals (Traps) and choose-it-or-not (SQS SNS or EventBridge table); also 2-deep.md Go deeper 'archive and replay', cards c014, speak s01
findings.quote: **Wrong belief:** An event bus keeps its events for later reads. **Truth:** Events are [not retained. To keep events, add an archive.](../facts/eventbridge.md#eventbridge-classic-bus-does-not-retain-events)
findings.type: claims: link scope narrower than the sentence; missing Changed recently note (RULINGS rule 7)
findings.evidence: The linked fact eventbridge-classic-bus-does-not-retain-events is scoped 'EventBridge Custom Event Bus - Classic'; its own source eb-custom-bus-what-is says: "The EventBridge Custom Event Bus ... keeps a copy of every event for a retention period that you set on the bus" and "Retention of every event for 1 to 365 days, set on the bus." The change feed (changes:eventbridge.jsonl, 2026-09-24, 'Amazon EventBridge relaunches event buses for enterprise scale'): "Custom event buses include 24 hours of built-in retention that can be extended for up to one year ... we have renamed the existing bus to Custom event bus - classic." So the unscoped truth 'An event bus ... Events are not retained', the compare cell 'EventBridge | Nothing: events are not retained' and Recap 1 'SNS and EventBridge keep nothing' are false for the current Custom Event Bus. The chapter uses the word 'Classic' (2-deep Go deeper, card c014, s01 must_not_say) without ever saying what the other bus type is, and it has no Changed recently note for the relaunch (new bus: retention, FIFO order per event group, publish-time dedup, RAM sharing, one target per subscriber). Fix: scope the statements to 'a rules-based (Classic) event bus, the type the exam uses', and add a Changed recently note: 2026-09-24, old: event buses keep nothing, now: the new Custom Event Bus retains events 1 to 365 days, status: not examinable yet (GA after 2026-07-15). This needs facts from eb-custom-bus-what-is (already in the corpus).
findings.resolution: fix-31: every retention statement is scoped to the Classic bus: 1-fast compare cell 'A Classic bus, nothing', trap Truth 'On a Classic bus, events are not retained...', Recap 1 'A Classic event bus: ...' (card c014 and s01 must_not_say were already scoped). The new bus is taught in 2-deep Go deeper 'archive and replay': 'A new Custom event bus of [2026-09-24] keeps events for [1 to 365 days]. It is not examinable yet.' (verified fact eventbridge-change-custom-event-bus-classic-rename-2026). Not done as a Changed recently callout: that fact has changed = null, so L107's date rule (entry date = changed.date of the Now: fact) cannot pass; no new fact was registered in the fix stage.

findings.section: recap (Recap 1); also choose-it-or-not table cell 'Nothing: messages are not persisted', Traps line on SNS, card c011, speak s01 kp2 and must_not_say
findings.quote: SQS keeps the message [until successfully processed or expired](../facts/sqs.md#sqs-decision-keeps-until-processed). SNS and EventBridge keep nothing.
findings.type: claims: unlinked absolute claim, refuted by AWS pages
findings.evidence: 'SNS and EventBridge keep nothing' has no fact link and is false. SNS: docs/sns/latest/dg/fifo-message-archiving-replay: "Amazon SNS provides a no-code message archiving and replay feature, specifically designed for FIFO (First-In-First-Out) topics. This feature allows topic owners to store messages directly within the topic archive for up to 365 days and replay them to subscribers when needed." Its first use case is "Message recovery - Recover messages lost due to downstream application failures by replaying them to the subscriber's endpoint." SNS documentation history: "Support added for message archiving and replay ... Topic owners can archive messages to a topic for up to 365 days ... October 26, 2023" (examinable, changed after mid-2022, no Changed recently note in the chapter). EventBridge: the chapter itself teaches archives (Q13 answer 'Create an archive of the event bus that keeps events for 30 days'), and the new Custom Event Bus retains events (claims-03). The same universal appears in card c011 ('No. SNS messages are not persisted'), speak s01 kp2 ('SNS ... does not persist messages', accept 'SNS keeps nothing') and the s01 must_not_say correction. Fix: scope to standard topics and Classic buses ('A standard SNS topic keeps nothing; a FIFO topic can archive messages for replay'), add a Changed recently note for SNS FIFO archive and replay (2023-10-26, examinable), and register a fact for it from fifo-message-archiving-replay.
findings.resolution: fix-31: the unlinked universal is removed. Recap 1 now: 'A standard SNS topic: [messages are not persisted]. A Classic event bus: [not retained. To keep events, add an archive.]'; compare cell 'A standard topic, nothing'; SNS trap Truth 'In a standard topic, ...' plus 'A FIFO topic can archive messages for [up to 365 days]' (verified fact sns-change-fifo-archiving-replay-2023, already in the canon); 2-deep step 3 'In a standard topic, messages are not persisted'; card c011 front 'does a standard topic keep...'; s01 kp2 point, accept ('SNS does not store messages for later'), line 7 and must_not_say correction scoped to a standard topic. No Changed recently entry: the archive fact has changed = null (L107 date rule) and the 1-fast section is at its 120-word cap.

findings.quote: Why copies? They keep the queue fast: it supports a [nearly unlimited number of API calls per second](../facts/sqs.md#sqs-standard-throughput-nearly-unlimited).

AWS gives redundancy and availability as the reason for copies, not speed; the throughput link only supports the number of API calls. Fix: 'Why copies? For redundancy and high availability: [for redundancy and high availability](../facts/sqs.md#sqs-copies-on-multiple-servers-cause-duplicates).' (check the fact's displays first).

findings.section: how (An SNS topic pushes each published message to all its subscribers, Stop and answer; and Failed deliveries are retried..., intro sentence)
findings.quote: Yes. The function's messages are lost: [messages are not persisted](../facts/sns.md#sns-decision-no-persistence).
findings.type: technical: right answer, wrong mechanism (contradicts the chapter's own retry numbers)
findings.evidence: docs/sns/latest/dg/sns-dead-letter-queues: "Client-side errors can happen when Amazon SNS has stale subscription metadata. These errors commonly occur when an owner deletes the endpoint (for example, a Lambda function subscribed to an Amazon SNS topic) ... Amazon SNS doesn't retry the message delivery that fails because of a client-side error." The same chapter says SNS tries Lambda '100,015 times' (fact sns-retry-aws-managed-total-attempts: 'over 23 days'), so a reader who reasons from the given answer would expect a one-week outage to be covered by retries. The loss happens because a deleted endpoint is a client-side error with no retry (unless a subscription dead-letter queue exists). The section intro 'SNS and EventBridge push, so each retries a failed delivery and then drops it' has the same gap for SNS (the EventBridge table already shows the no-retry errors). Fix: answer 'Yes. A deleted function is a client-side error: SNS does not retry it and discards the message unless the subscription has a dead-letter queue', with a new fact from sns-dead-letter-queues; add a 'Deleted endpoint or changed policy: no retry' row for SNS.
findings.resolution: fix-31: Stop and answer is now 'A topic's Lambda subscriber is deleted and created again a week later. Did it miss that week's messages?' Answer: 'Yes. The delivery [fails because of a client-side error](sns-client-side-error-not-retried), which SNS does not retry, so the retries [over 23 days] do not apply.' The retries table now has the row 'SNS: deleted endpoint | No: it fails because of a client-side error'. The dead-letter clause for client-side errors was not added: its fact (sns-faq-message-discarded-after-retries-unless-dlq-attached) is not verified.

findings.section: how (Queues subscribed to a topic give each consumer its own durable copy, step 3)
findings.quote: A subscription with a filter policy gets a message only when the message attributes [satisfy the conditions specified in the filter policy](../facts/sns.md#sns-filter-nonmatching-message-not-sent).
findings.type: claims: condition dropped from the fact
findings.evidence: Fact sns-filter-nonmatching-message-not-sent quote (sns-message-filtering): "If all of the message attributes or message body properties satisfy the conditions specified in the filter policy, Amazon SNS sends the message to the subscriber." The sentence narrows filtering to message attributes; payload (message body) filtering exists and is priced (fact sns-pricing-attribute-filtering-free: "payload-based message filtering is based on the total amount of outbound payload data scanned"). A reader would wrongly reject an option that filters SNS messages on body fields. Fix: 'when the message attributes or the message body [satisfy ...]'.
findings.resolution: fix-31: step 3 now reads 'when the message attributes or the message body satisfy ...'; the same text is in the say of step 3 of diagrams/src/messaging-fanout.json (L703), SVG rebuilt with diagram build.

findings.quote: "extra": "An encrypted queue behind an SNS subscription needs a custom KMS key."
findings.type: claims: scope of the fact dropped (overgeneralized)
findings.evidence: The cited fact sns-dlq-encrypted-queue-needs-custom-kms-key is scoped 'SNS subscription dead-letter queue with SSE-KMS'; quote: "To use an encrypted Amazon SQS queue as a dead-letter queue, you must use a custom KMS with a key policy that grants the Amazon SNS service principal access to AWS KMS API actions." The card drops both conditions (dead-letter queue, SSE-KMS). An SSE-SQS-encrypted queue receives from SNS with no KMS key at all, which the chapter's own Q2 relies on (the SSE-SQS option is rejected only because the company must control a key policy). Fix: 'A queue with SSE-KMS behind an SNS subscription needs a customer managed key whose policy allows SNS.' and cite sqs-kms-service-senders-need-customer-managed-key or sns-sse-topic-to-encrypted-queue-needs-cmk-policy.
findings.resolution: fix-31: c029 extra now 'For SNS to deliver to a queue encrypted with AWS KMS, use a customer managed key whose policy allows SNS.'; facts now sqs-kms-aws-managed-key-policy-not-modifiable and sns-sse-topic-to-encrypted-queue-needs-cmk-policy.

findings.quote: Fix it: add a queue policy that lets this one topic send messages to this queue. Then run the publish command of step 5 again.
findings.type: technical: task step can fail falsely (propagation delay)
findings.evidence: docs/cli/latest/reference/sqs/set-queue-attributes: "When you change a queue's attributes, the change can take up to 60 seconds for most of the attributes to propagate throughout the Amazon SQS system." The reader publishes right after set-queue-attributes; if the policy has not propagated, SNS delivery fails with a client-side error that SNS does not retry (sns-dead-letter-queues: "Amazon SNS doesn't retry the message delivery that fails because of a client-side error"), and step 8 shows no message although the fix is correct. findings.quote: The AWS service and the application send to the default event bus and a custom event bus; the SaaS partner sends to a partner event bus. Each bus has rules
findings.type: claims: diagram text contradicts the drawing and the fact
findings.evidence: Fact eventbridge-aws-service-events-go-to-default-bus: "When an AWS service in your account sends an event to EventBridge, it goes to your account's default event bus." The spec's edges are aws -> defbus and app -> cusbus only, and the custom bus has no rule (its edge goes to 'No action'). The alt says AWS service events reach a custom bus and that every bus has rules. A screen-reader or caption-only reader learns a wrong routing fact. Fix: 'An AWS service sends to the default event bus, your application to a custom event bus, and the SaaS partner to a partner event bus. The default and partner buses have rules; an event on the custom bus matches no rule.'
findings.resolution: fix-31: spec alt and the Markdown alt now say the AWS service sends to the default bus, the application to a custom bus, the SaaS partner to a partner bus; rules on the default and partner buses point to targets; an event on the custom bus matches no rule. SVG rebuilt.

findings.section: how (A standard queue can deliver a message twice so consumers must be idempotent, table)
findings.quote: | Add a credit | The balance is wrong | It skips a message ID it has seen |
findings.type: technical: weak practice that contradicts the chapter's own best practice
findings.evidence: Fact sqs-consumers-keep-idempotency-tokens-ignore-duplicates (REL04-BP04): "When a publisher generates and includes idempotency tokens in messages ... Consumers should keep track of each token received and ignore messages that contain duplicate tokens." The chapter's Stop-and-answer uses this token, and Q7 (messaging-q004) deduplicates on the business order ID with a conditional write. A producer that retries SendMessage creates a new message with a new SQS message ID, so skipping seen message IDs misses those duplicates (Q7's 'partner sends the same order again' case). Fix: 'It skips an idempotency token (for example the order ID) it has seen'.
findings.resolution: fix-31: table cell now 'It skips an idempotency token, such as the order ID, that it has seen'.

findings.section: how (A FIFO queue keeps order inside each message group and drops duplicates, step 3)
findings.quote: **Deduplicate.** A repeat in the [5 minute deduplication interval](../facts/sqs.md#sqs-fifo-deduplication-interval-5-minutes) is dropped
findings.type: claims: condition dropped (what counts as a repeat)
findings.evidence: Fact sqs-fifo-deduplication-interval-5-minutes: "If multiple messages with the same deduplication ID are sent within a 5 minute deduplication interval, they are treated as duplicates". A 'repeat' is a message with the same deduplication ID (given by the producer, or the body hash with content-based deduplication, facts sqs-fifo-content-based-dedup-hash-body-only / sqs-fifo-generated-dedup-id-from-body-hash). The same body sent with a new deduplication ID is not dropped. Fix: 'A message with the same deduplication ID inside the 5 minute deduplication interval is dropped'.
findings.resolution: fix-31: step 3 now 'A message with the same message deduplication ID inside the [5 minute deduplication interval] is dropped', plus 'Content-based deduplication can make this ID [by hashing the message body](sqs-fifo-generated-dedup-id-from-body-hash).'

findings.section: how (Resource-based policies decide which accounts and services may send to a queue)
findings.quote: Why the resource's policy? The [queue owner pays](../facts/sqs.md#sqs-faq-queue-owner-pays-for-shared-access) for shared access, so the owner decides.
findings.evidence: Fact sqs-faq-queue-owner-pays-for-shared-access: "The message queue owner pays for shared message queue access." It says nothing about why access is decided by the resource policy. The reason is cross-account evaluation: fact iam-eval-cross-account-needs-both-policies ("allows the request only if both evaluations return Allow"), used in Q18. Fix: 'Why the resource's policy? The queue belongs to its owner's account, and a call from another account needs an Allow in both accounts.'
findings.resolution: fix-31: invented causal link removed. Now 'Why the resource's policy? For a call from another account, AWS [allows the request only if both evaluations return Allow](iam-eval-cross-account-needs-both-policies): the caller's policy and the queue's policy.'
